newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SDP COUNCIL SAYS TO CONSIDER EMU IN SEPT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SDP COUNCIL SAYS TO CONSIDER EMU IN SEPT.

text.p: The council of Finland's Social democratic Party (SDP) -- the biggest in parliament and government -- will consider its stance on EMU at an extraordinary meeting in September, SDP said on Wednesday.
A draft resolution expected to be adopted -- but which might also be changed -- by the council later in the day was made available to Reuters.
"The party council will consider the EMU issue in September at an extraordinary meeting," SDP said in a statement.
Party leader, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen, is openly in favour of Finnish membership of EMU from the start in 1999.
According to the draft resolution, SDP believed that conditions exist to create new jobs.
"Conditions exist for the creation of new jobs," it said.
"Economic growth creates new jobs," it added. Lipponen earlier told the council that sustained economic growth was in sight as far as forecasts reached.

In taxation, the target should be to lower income taxes and social security contributions, and develop value-added taxation, so that demand for labour would increase, particularly in labour-intensive sectors, the party said.
"Tax relief in 1998-99 must be targetted primarily at low-wage earners to reach the best possible increase in employment," the draft resolution said.
"The emphasis in income tax and social security contribution reductions must be on low incomes," it said, adding VAT should be cut in sectors offering personal services.
"Tax and social security contribution changes in 1998-99 should be dimensioned so that the decline in state indebtedness is not endangered," SDP said.
Turning to energy issues, the draft resolution said decisions should be based on the use and development of many sources of energy.
"All central options must be compared for the baseload power production decisions," SDP said.

"The decisions must consider the availability of energy, a moderate price, employment and environmental effects and energy savings targets," it added. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
